items_missed: No 'How are you today?' warmth check, and no agenda statement or explicit 'sound good?' framing before jumping into questions.
Never asked about additional rooms (garage/storage/balcony), storage stops, additional stops, access concerns (elevator, parking, HOA), or 'anything you're worried about with this move?'
No 'Pricing is super simple' opener, and didn't explain what's included in the hourly rate (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools).
No mention of No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover email, or On-Time Guarantee — all three core differentiators were left out entirely.
Never explained the clock mechanics — no mention of the 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute prorated increments, or when the clock starts on-site.

Gave a generic 'full pack takes ~8 hours' estimate but didn't explain how stairs, additional stops, drive time/trip fee (move is ~50 miles away), or walk distance could move that number, and never gave a truck count.
Skipped the Save Your Ass prep speech entirely — no consolidation tips, no 'take a carload' advice — at the exact moment the customer was trying to shrink her own bill by estimating hours herself.

Never mentioned sending a confirmation email, the bolded details list, or 'reply with any corrections'; never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave hours or how to reach the branch.
Never used the customer's name (Christina) after getting it.
Re-asked a question the customer had already answered (current floor), which visibly frustrated her ('I literally just said that... like sixty seconds ago').
No insurance explanation (No Worries + 60 cents/lb baseline) despite a damage-adjacent moment (bed reassembly).
Answered questions reactively throughout (cost, reassembly, bicycles) rather than raising FAQs proactively.
top_strength: Zachary stayed calm and clear when the customer pushed back on price, walking her through the per-mover hourly math step by step and reassuring her she only pays for time actually worked, which resolved her budget worry and got a verbal booking commitment for the 19th.
coaching_note: The customer was actively trying to estimate and shrink her own bill mid-call ('I was thinking it'd be a thousand... that just takes off the three hours') — that's precisely the cue for the Save Your Ass prep speech (pre-pack consolidation tips, 'take a carload'), which Zachary skipped entirely; leading with it before pricing would have anchored her expectations instead of leaving her to guess.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and steady throughout, including a reasonable recovery after visibly annoying the customer with a repeated question, but the call stayed transactional with almost no affirming or empathetic language.
